result.title: LiBRA: Logit Fingerprints for Byzantine-Robust Client Selection in Federated Learning
result.summary: Byzantine-robust aggregation shields federated learning from malicious updates, but the rules that filter out suspect updates do so by comparing clients' parameter vectors. That comparison requires access to every client's update, which secure aggregation exists to withhold, costs $O(n^2 d)$ in the parameter dimension $d$, and is defined only between clients that share an architecture. We propose LiBRA, which compares clients on what their models compute rather than on the parameters that compute them, using a fingerprint of $C^2$ values for $C$ classes, the class-conditional logit response of each client's model to pseudo-patterns optimised against it. We instantiate LiBRA as variants of Krum, Multi-Krum and Bulyan that change only what the dissimilarity score is computed on. On Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 with three architectures and four backdoor and label-manipulation attacks under i.i.d. partitions, each variant holds every attack its parent holds, and on identical client updates under a backdoor attack the fingerprint ranks malicious clients within 0.006 AUC of the full parameter vector. The variants thus match the robustness of the rules they extend, while their trust decision reads no client parameter, compares up to 49,090 times fewer values, and can by construction compare clients whose architectures differ, at the cost of one pattern optimisation per client per round.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LiBRA，以针对每个客户端模型优化出的伪模式所引发的类条件 logit 响应（C² 维指纹）替代参数向量作为客户端间差异度量，并将其实例化为 Krum、Multi-Krum、Bulyan 的变体，在 Fashion-MNIST 与 CIFAR-10 上评测后门与标签操纵攻击下的鲁棒性和比较开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 用优化伪输入探测模型「计算了什么」而得到紧凑函数签名，可能为 LVR 中检测视觉证据是否真正进入输出、或跨模型比较 latent 内容提供轻量探针线索；需核查该指纹反映的是内容而非训练痕迹。
